checks.question: Is the source the one that the site describes?
checks.note: The site build records the commit of this repository. The record of the Lean build records the commit of tamnd/singularity-lean and the pin of the base. The check that refuses a mismatch is planned.

checks.question: Does it build?
checks.note: The workflows build and base of tamnd/singularity-lean build the packages Singularity and SingularityBase at Lean v4.35.0 on GitHub runners, at commit 3b63a7b. The base job restores the build of resolutionorg/hironaka from a cache keyed by its pin and the toolchain.

checks.question: Which axioms do the top theorems use?
checks.note: 1937 declarations in records/lean.json. Each uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The scan finds no sorry, admit or axiom in the project source.

checks.question: Does a second kernel accept it?
checks.note: Run 45319996607 of the trust workflow of tamnd/singularity-lean, at commit e6e585d, has these results. leanchecker --fresh replays the environments of Singularity and SingularityBase in the kernel of Lean, and both pass. nanoda, a type checker for Lean written in Rust, checks the export of Singularity with all the declarations that it uses, Mathlib included, and it passes. nanoda is a separate implementation with its own design. The comparator job also runs the bundled checkers lean4lean and nanoda on the proved theorems, and they pass. The job that runs lean4lean on each module of Singularity did not give a result: in two runs the hosted runner lost communication with the server, which is a fault of the runner and not a rejection by lean4lean. An earlier run, 45271857389 at commit 665b516, passed this job. On a project server, lean4lean also checked each of the 43 modules of Singularity at commit ce778c3, one module at a time, and it accepted each of them. The run on the root module Singularity, which has no declarations of its own, was stopped by the system when the server was out of memory. The modules that came after commit ce778c3 are not in this check. A person must still decide if these checks are sufficient.

checks.question: Do the proved theorems have the pinned statements?
checks.note: manifests/statements.sha256 pins the statement files, and CI checks the hashes. In run 45319996607 at commit e6e585d, lake comparator --paranoid checks the theorems of Singularity against comparator/Challenge.lean, which states them again from Singularity/Statements/. It passes: the statements are the same, the axioms are only propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice, and the kernel and the bundled checkers accept the proofs. The comparator builds and exports the code in a bwrap sandbox. The same check for the base package passes, but it runs with --inadvisably-no-sandbox, because the base package depends on Singularity at the path .. and the sandbox binds only the directory base. The checks are the same, but the build is not isolated.

checks.question: Do the statements mean what the docstrings say?
checks.note: Fidelity checks F2 (the identity of a regular scheme) and F3 (the codiagonal) are proved. The bridge to formal-conjectures is proved in one direction. The other instances of the battery are planned.

checks.question: Which published theorems are still hypotheses?
checks.note: None. The last one, ReductionToIntegral (SG0000001Y), is proved by Singularity.Reduction.reductionToIntegral. The theorems resolutionInDim_charZero (SG0000000D) and Curves.resolutionInDim_one (SG0000001A) use it and take no hypothesis.

checks.question: Has a person read the proof?
checks.note: The handbook sections are at status drafted. No reviewer has signed them.

checks.question: Has someone outside the project reproduced Q1 to Q4?
